findings.evidence: writeAll() originally called Asset.create()+assetRepository.save() directly, duplicating AssetService.createAsset()'s logic, based on an incorrect assumption that going through AssetOperations would break transactional atomicity.
findings.why_it_matters: Splitting Asset-creation logic across two call sites creates drift risk; the underlying atomicity concern was also based on a misunderstanding of Spring's REQUIRED propagation (it joins the caller's open transaction rather than starting a new one).
findings.required_action: Inject AssetOperations and call assetOperations.createAsset(new CreateAssetRequest(...)) instead of touching AssetRepository/Asset.create() directly.

findings.evidence: The extension-inferred audio MIME type (probeAudioMimeType) was never checked against AUDIO_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES before upload, unlike the single-question audio upload path.
findings.why_it_matters: Unrecognized-extension audio files would upload with content-type application/octet-stream, potentially preventing browser playback, with no validation error surfaced to the importer.
findings.required_action: Add a row-validation check rejecting rows whose probeAudioMimeType(audioFilename) is absent from AUDIO_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES, collected alongside other row errors.
